hints: Resolve each force along the $x$-axis: the $24\text{ N}$ force has component $+24\cos 25^\circ$ and the $12\text{ N}$ force has component $-12\cos 65^\circ$.
Resolve each force along the $y$-axis: the $30\text{ N}$ force acts purely in the $+y$ direction, while the other two have downward components.
walkthrough:
Resolve all forces in the horizontal ($x$) direction:
$$R_x = 24\cos 25^\circ - 12\cos 65^\circ$$
$$R_x = 24(0.906308) - 12(0.422618) = 21.7514 - 5.0714 = 16.6800\text{ N} \approx 16.7\text{ N}$$

Resolve all forces in the vertical ($y$) direction:
$$R_y = 30 - 24\sin 25^\circ - 12\sin 65^\circ$$
$$R_y = 30 - 24(0.422618) - 12(0.906308) = 30 - 10.1428 - 10.8757 = 8.9815\text{ N} \approx 8.98\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for the resultant component along the $x$-axis:
$$R_x = \Sigma F_x$$
Identify the horizontal contributions:
- The $24\text{ N}$ force acts at $25^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis: $+24\cos 25^\circ$.
- The $12\text{ N}$ force acts at $65^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis: $-12\cos 65^\circ$.
- The $30\text{ N}$ force acts vertically upwards, contributing $0$ along $x$.

Calculate $R_x$ numerically:
$$R_x = 24\cos 25^\circ - 12\cos 65^\circ$$
Evaluate trigonometric ratios:
$$\cos 25^\circ \approx 0.906308, \quad \cos 65^\circ \approx 0.422618$$
$$24 \times 0.906308 = 21.75139\text{ N}$$
$$12 \times 0.422618 = 5.07142\text{ N}$$
$$R_x = 21.75139 - 5.07142 = 16.67997\text{ N} \approx 16.7\text{ N}$$

State the formula for the resultant component along the $y$-axis:
$$R_y = \Sigma F_y$$
Identify the vertical contributions:
- The $30\text{ N}$ force acts purely upwards: $+30\text{ N}$.
- The $24\text{ N}$ force acts downwards: $-24\sin 25^\circ$.
- The $12\text{ N}$ force acts downwards: $-12\sin 65^\circ$.

Calculate $R_y$ numerically:
$$R_y = 30 - 24\sin 25^\circ - 12\sin 65^\circ$$
Evaluate trigonometric ratios:
$$\sin 25^\circ \approx 0.422618, \quad \sin 65^\circ \approx 0.906308$$
$$24 \times 0.422618 = 10.14283\text{ N}$$
$$12 \times 0.906308 = 10.87570\text{ N}$$
$$R_y = 30 - 10.14283 - 10.87570 = 30 - 21.01853 = 8.98147\text{ N} \approx 8.98\text{ N}$$

hints: Both $R_x > 0$ and $R_y > 0$, so the resultant lies in the first quadrant.
Use $\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x}$ to find the angle $\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis.
walkthrough: Since both $R_x = 16.6800\text{ N} > 0$ and $R_y = 8.9815\text{ N} > 0$, the resultant vector lies in the first quadrant.

Find the angle $\theta$ with the positive $x$-direction:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x} = \frac{8.9815}{16.6800} \approx 0.53846$$
$$\theta = \arctan(0.53846) \approx 28.30^\circ \approx 28.3^\circ$$
The direction is $28.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-direction (or above the positive $x$-axis).
teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the quadrant of the resultant vector:
With $R_x = +16.67997\text{ N}$ (positive) and $R_y = +8.98147\text{ N}$ (positive), the resultant points upwards and to the right in the first quadrant.

State the formula for the directional angle $\theta$ measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x}$$

Substitute the unrounded component values:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{8.98147}{16.67997} \approx 0.538458$$
Calculate the inverse tangent:
$$\theta = \arctan(0.538458) \approx 28.3003^\circ$$
Rounding to 1 decimal place gives $28.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from the positive $x$-direction.
